hrs.settings.device.label: Heart rate monitor
hrs.settings.device.description: Leave empty to connect to the first monitor found. Picking a suggestion fills in "name [address]". A name on its own also works.
hrs.settings.noSignalSeconds.label: Seconds before counting as no signal
hrs.settings.noSignalSeconds.description: If no heart rate arrives for this long, the avatar is told it has stopped.
hrs.settings.reconnectSeconds.label: Reconnect interval (seconds)
hrs.settings.reconnectSeconds.descriptio: How long to wait before trying again when the monitor isn't found or the connection drops.
hrs.settings.recordingEnabled.label: Record heart rate
hrs.settings.recordingEnabled.descriptio: Stores every heart rate received in a database, one row each. You can export them to CSV from the hrs panel. Turning it off keeps what is already stored.
hrs.settings.oscPreset.label: OSC preset
hrs.settings.oscPreset.description: Which set of parameters is sent to the avatar. Pick the one whose names your avatar listens for: VRCHR sends names such as onesHR and isHRBeat, VRCOSC sends the names under VRCOSC/Heartrate/ that VRCOSC's heart rate module uses.
hrs.settings.smoothValues.label: Smooth the values
hrs.settings.smoothValues.description: Moves the heart rate and the average that are sent towards each new reading over about a second. When off, each reading is sent as it arrives. The beat timing does not change.
hrs.settings.hds.label: Receive from Apple Watch (HDS)
hrs.settings.hds.description: Receives the heart rate that Health Data Server (the Apple Watch app) sends over the LAN. The monitor and the watch can be used at once; whichever arrives first is used. Windows asks about the firewall the first time this listens; if you declined, the hrs panel can fix it.
hrs.settings.hds.port.label: Listening port
hrs.settings.hds.port.description: The port you enter in the watch app, together with this PC's IP. Defaults to the standard HDS port.
hrs.settings.hds.firewall.label: Firewall
hrs.settings.hds.firewall.description: Shows whether Windows Firewall lets the watch reach this PC. A rule is added only when you press the button.
hrs.settings.hds.firewall.offDetail: Checked once you turn on receiving from Apple Watch and apply.
hrs.settings.hds.firewall.presentDetail: A firewall rule allows TCP {0}, the HDS (Apple Watch) port.
hrs.settings.hds.firewall.failedDetail: Failed to read the Windows Firewall settings. If nothing arrives from the watch, allow incoming TCP {0} in the firewall.
hrs.settings.hds.noSignalSeconds.label: Seconds before counting as no signal
hrs.settings.hds.noSignalSeconds.descrip: How long to wait after the watch goes quiet before counting it as stopped. HealthKit sends every 5 seconds and pauses for tens of seconds when your wrist is down, so this waits longer than for the monitor above.
hrs.settings.broadcast.label: Broadcast (WebSocket / overlays)
hrs.settings.broadcast.description: Opens a port for OBS overlays and for outside tools that read the heart rate. It stays on this PC and is not reachable from the LAN. Another app on the same port clashes with it, so stop one of them or change the port.
hrs.settings.broadcast.port.label: Port
hrs.settings.broadcast.port.description: The port in the overlay URLs.
hrs.settings.zones.label: Zone thresholds
hrs.settings.zones.description: Where the zones shown on the overlays (rest / light / moderate / hard) begin. A heart rate at or above each value falls in that zone. Resting heart rate varies between people, so you can adjust them to suit you.
hrs.settings.zones.light.label: light
hrs.settings.zones.moderate.label: moderate
hrs.settings.zones.hard.label: hard
hrs.settings.parameters.label: VRCHR parameter names
hrs.settings.parameters.description: The names the VRCHR preset sends. /avatar/parameters/ is added to each when sending.
hrs.settings.parameters.ones.label: Ones digit
hrs.settings.parameters.tens.label: Tens digit
hrs.settings.parameters.hundreds.label: Hundreds digit
hrs.settings.parameters.isActive.label: Active
hrs.settings.parameters.isActive.descrip: Whether beats are arriving. False whenever the heart rate is 0 (disconnected, silent for a while, or not measuring).
hrs.settings.parameters.isBeat.label: Beat
hrs.settings.parameters.percent.label: Heart rate ratio
hrs.settings.parameters.percent.descript: A 0-1 float: the heart rate divided by 255.
hrs.settings.parameters.fullPercent.desc: Sends the same value under another name.
hrs.settings.parameters.heartRate.label: Heart rate value
hrs.settings.vrcosc.label: VRCOSC parameter names
hrs.settings.vrcosc.description: The names the VRCOSC preset sends. /avatar/parameters/ is added to each when sending. The defaults match VRCOSC's heart rate module.
hrs.settings.vrcosc.connected.label: Connected
hrs.settings.vrcosc.connected.descriptio: Whether beats are arriving. False whenever the heart rate is 0.
hrs.settings.vrcosc.value.label: Heart rate
hrs.settings.vrcosc.value.description: The heart rate as an integer.
hrs.settings.vrcosc.normalised.label: Normalised
hrs.settings.vrcosc.normalised.descripti: A 0-1 float: the heart rate mapped from 0-240.
hrs.settings.vrcosc.average.label: Average
hrs.settings.vrcosc.average.description: The average of the heart rates received in the last 10 seconds, as an integer.
hrs.settings.vrcosc.beat.label: Beat
hrs.settings.vrcosc.beat.description: Flips between true and false on every beat. False when stopped.
hrs.settings.vrcosc.enabled.label: Connected (legacy)
hrs.settings.vrcosc.enabled.description: Sends the same value as Connected under the older name.
hrs.settings.vrcosc.units.label: Ones digit (legacy)
hrs.settings.vrcosc.tens.label: Tens digit (legacy)
hrs.settings.vrcosc.hundreds.label: Hundreds digit (legacy)
hrs.settings.vrcosc.digit.description: That digit divided by 10, as a float (7 becomes 0.7).
hrs.panel.title: Current heart rate
hrs.panel.device.hint: Pick one under "Heart rate monitor" in settings, or leave it empty to use the first one found.
hrs.panel.heldOff: It won't reconnect until you press Connect.
hrs.panel.stopped: Stopped. The avatar has been told it is not connected.
hrs.panel.history.hint: Drag to zoom in / double-click to step back / right-click for the whole day / wheel to zoom in and out (down to 10 seconds)
hrs.panel.devices.title: Monitors found
hrs.panel.devices.empty: No monitors found yet. Turn the monitor on and wait a moment.
hrs.panel.devices.hint: Only devices broadcasting the heart rate service are listed. Signal strength (dBm) is stronger the closer it is to 0.
hrs.panel.hds.title: Apple Watch (HDS)
hrs.panel.hds.hint: Enter this address and port in the Apple Watch app (Health Data Server).
hrs.panel.hds.none: No LAN address found. Check that this PC is connected to a network.
hrs.panel.firewall.missing: No firewall rule allows TCP {0}, the HDS (Apple Watch) port. If nothing arrives from the watch, this is why.
hrs.panel.firewall.blocked: A firewall rule blocks TCP {0}, the HDS (Apple Watch) port (pressing Cancel on the Windows prompt creates it). A block wins over an allow, so the watch can't reach this PC until it is removed.
hrs.panel.ws.title: Broadcast
hrs.panel.ws.off: Broadcasting is off. Turn on "Broadcast" in settings to get URLs you can paste into OBS.
hrs.panel.ws.failed: Failed to listen on port {0}. Check whether another app is using the same port ({1})
hrs.panel.ws.overlays: URLs for an OBS browser source
hrs.panel.records.title: Records
hrs.panel.records.off: Recording is off. Turn on "Record heart rate" in settings.
hrs.panel.records.range.view: The range shown on the graph
hrs.error.badAddress: '{0}' isn't a valid address. Enter it as AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF, or remove the [] and use the device name instead
hrs.error.zoneOrder: Zone thresholds must go light < moderate < hard
hrs.error.paramName.slash: cannot start or end with /, or contain //
hrs.name: Heart rate
